Role: Hybrid support/melee. Difficulty: Medium. Weapon: Staff (block-capable, no shield swap needed).

SupportMelee hybridGroup-dependent

blocks.title: Overview and role
blocks.bodyHtml:
Chanter is a melee support/healer hybrid, strong in groups but its unique value is wasted playing solo.

Version note: AION 2 has been live in KR/TW since November 2025. Global PC launch is October 5, 2026, with a fully wiped Launch Scale Test on September 17-18. Nearly all Chanter guides below are KR/TW-era. A reported August 2026 balance patch removed fixed healing passives in favor of attack-power-scaling healing, which one source says dropped Chanter to C-tier alongside Cleric single source leprestore, date unknown1.
Possibly Aion 1: some search results for this class returned original-Aion fan wiki pages (aion.fandom.com, differ.blog, an aspirine.su stigma calculator) rather than AION 2 sources. Those are excluded from claims below except where explicitly flagged as a conflation risk.

Role and kit

Chanter is a hybrid support/melee class. AION2 Hub calls it a "Staff-wielding hybrid priest who buffs, heals, and fights on the front line" aion2hub, date unknown2.

Fextralife similarly describes it as a hybrid support that increases ally stats during party play and can function in several roles simultaneously, from buffer to a secondary healer or damage dealer fextralife, date unknown3.

Weapon: Staff. Unlike the original AION, Chanter can now block effectively with the staff itself, removing the old mace-and-shield swap so Staff is the single weapon for offense and defense single source.

Identity

AION2 Hub frames it precisely: Chanter is "never the main healer, yet able to keep a group standing while contributing real damage," trading peak healing output for survivability and offense, a "sustain-and-support bruiser" aion2hub, date unknown4.

Fextralife notes a mechanical limitation: the class lacks instant single-target heals but excels with AoE regeneration zones, and cites beta feedback calling it "a hybrid healer with high DPS and strong self-sustain" fextralife, date unknown5.

Difficulty, demand, and solo play

  • Difficulty and grade: one build-guide site rates Chanter Medium difficulty, PvE grade B, PvP grade B single source aion2boost, date unknown6
    • Caveat: "its grade is a function of your roster, not just your hands," over-performing in premades and merely hitting its stated B tier in solo queue.
  • Party demand: called "the clear top choice if your priority is party buffs." single source aggregation
    • Runs a Mantra-based toolkit with offensive, defensive, and utility benefits.
    • The build most players will expect for group content like dungeons, rift battles, world bosses, and guild raids. This contrasts with Cleric's more universal, role-agnostic demand.

Solo viability is contested between sources.

  • Fextralife says Chanter is "Great for soloing due to high DPS and Healing ability" with strong self-healing and survivability when playing solo fextralife, date unknown7
  • Other aggregated guides describe a "control bruiser" that thrives in solo play with fast mob clearing thanks to built-in sustain and crowd control marketing, lower trust
  • aion2boost.com is more skeptical: solo viability is "modest as a standalone bruiser" because the class struggles without allies to benefit from its buffs, making solo play less rewarding than group content aion2boost, date unknown8

Net read: Chanter solos fine numerically, but its unique value is wasted when alone.

Beginner tip: pick Chanter if you enjoy melee-range hybrid support and expect to run with a regular static group or guild. aion2boost.com's verdict: "Pick the Chanter if you play with regular groups; avoid it if exclusively solo queueing."

blocks.title: Skill priority
blocks.bodyHtml:
Rush Dark Wave, Hand of Recovery, Crushing Wave and Back Breaker to 20 first; the rest is synthesized from two guides that disagree in places.

Gap: no single confirmed global-launch SP order was found. The following synthesizes two KR-era Vortex Gaming guides, which disagree in places.
  1. Do first: reach level 20 on Dark Wave, Hand of Recovery, Crushing Wave, and Back Breaker. Dark Wave is the class's primary damage output; Crushing Wave is useful for both macro chains and animation canceling vortexgaming, date unknown1.
  2. Then: level Huyu's Spell to 16 (10% max HP recovery, 3-second cast-time reduction) vortexgaming, date unknown2
    • Level Gust Dance to 16 (on-hit, reduces all skill recast time by 1 second).
    • Level Heat Wave Strike to 16 (a successful block gives 25% chance to reset its recast time).
  3. Then: prioritize Charge Strike's 5-second recast reduction spec (it triggers Heat Wave Strike on a successful hit).
    • Prioritize Crushing Blow's HP-drain spec for survivability.
    • Prioritize Vibration Blow's range spec paired with the Raging Blow combo for bosses.
  4. Later / optional: Striking Blow as a combo filler for boss fights (its stun does not apply to bosses).
    • An Gyeok Se as an AoE skill paired with the Penetrating Blow combo for trash.
    • Shock Release specced for 20% HP recovery on cast, noted as "limited effectiveness in certain dungeons."

Two guides' passive order

Guide 1 passive order

  • First priority: Attack Preparation, Cocoon's Spell, Blessing of Life ("increases health and healing amplification"), Will to Survive, Promise of Wind, Spell of Path
  • Second priority: Cross Protection, Promise of Earth, Shock Hit vortexgaming, date unknown3

Guide 2 passive order

  • First-priority: Attack Preparation, Blessing of Life
  • Second-tier: Impact Hit, Inspiration Spell
  • Third priority: Promise of Earth, Promise of Wind single source

Attack Preparation and Blessing of Life are consistently top priority across both guides; the rest of the ordering is contested.

Because Chanter's healing kit is AoE regen zones rather than instant burst heal, guides suggest leveling Hand of Recovery / Huyu's Spell alongside your main damage chain (Dark Wave, Crushing Wave) rather than one before the other, since group-sustain and "real damage" are both core to the class per AION2 Hub's description aion2hub, date unknown4.

Gap: no reliable source found for a precise level-by-level SP order for Global launch, or a single unambiguous "ignore this skill early" list beyond the low-priority passives noted above.

blocks.title: Leveling build
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Lv 1 to cap contested kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Push Shatter Strike and Dark Strike to skill Lv 20, keep mantras running nonstop, then take Source of Invincibility as your first stigma.

This order is drawn from six Korean 호법성 community threads, mainly Inven and DCInside boards plus one FM Korea thread, not a single guide. Sources give the skill's own level, the 8/12/16/20 breakpoints, not your character level, unless a step names one.

Skill point order

StepWhenSkillTake toWhySrc
1From Lv 1Shatter Strike (격파쇄)Skill Lv 20most Chanter damage comes from weaving this between auto-attacksdcinside 990309, date unknown inven 11651, date unknown
2Alongside step 1Dark Strike (암격쇄)Skill Lv 20finisher on stunned or downed targets, boss cornerstone via CC-bypassinven 116, date unknown inven 11651, date unknown
3NextGale Barrage (질풍 난무)Skill Lv 16cooldown reduction for burst during groggy phasesinven 116, date unknown
4OngoingSpin Strike (회전격)secondary, no fixed target givenpairs with Shatter Strike's cooldown cut for the top DPS windowinven 31, date unknown fmkorea, date unknown
5Contested, see note belowHealing Incantation (쾌유의 주문)Skill Lv 16 (best supported) or 20 (single-source alternative)party/self sustain, near-mandatory in group content either waydcinside 990309, date unknown

No source names a Chanter skill to leave at skill Lv 1 outright. The closest claim is that nothing except Shatter Strike and Dark Strike needs to reach 20 inven 11651, date unknown1, so the "leave at level 1" block is dropped here.

Passives

  1. First: Attack Preparation (공격 준비), top priority across all three sources that gave a passive order inven 116, date unknown2 dcinside 371687, date unknown3
  2. Then: Promise of Wind (바람의 약속) for crit damage and Impact Hit (충격 적중) for stun confirmation, both ranked high across sources fmkorea, date unknown4
  3. Later: Blessing of Life (생명의 축복), roughly +30% HP and +21% healing amplification, ranked lower by one source but present in all three dcinside 371687, date unknown5
Protection Ward (보호진) splits opinion: one guide calls it worth taking for its auto-triggering party shield, another says skip it since its internal cooldown undercuts stacking inven 116, date unknown6 dcinside 371687, date unknown7.

Level by level

  1. Lv 1-12
    Weave Shatter Strike as your constant filler, save Dark Strike for finishers

    Chanter levels as a melee damage dealer, not a healer. One source states it outright: "호법은 '딜러'입니다" (Chanter is a DPS) inven 11651, date unknown8.

    • Keep mantras running the whole time. English guides name them Speed Mantra, Healing Mantra, Valor Mantra; Korean sources name the mantra stigmas 질주의 진언, 쾌유의 진언, 불패의 진언, and the English names do not map cleanly onto them u4n, date unknown9
  2. Lv 12
    Daevanion board opens

    Same shared system as every class; see the Daevanion board route card below for node priority vortexgaming, date unknown10.

  3. Lv 23
    Stigma: Source of Invincibility (불패의 진언) first, no argument

    Called mandatory for +25% damage amplification and +25% damage resistance inven 116, date unknown11.

    • Defensive cooldown pick: Focused Defense (집중 방어) grants a 3-second block stance that blocks everything "except instant-death mechanics" single source inven 116, date unknown12
    • Alternative: base Block (막기), which one guide reframes from a defensive tool into an offensive uptime enabler single source dcinside 990309, date unknown13
  4. Lv 23-45
    Boss fights: hold both attacks down, weave in a groggy-trigger skill reactively

    Spin Strike pairs with Shatter Strike's cooldown cut for the highest sustained DPS window inven 31, date unknown14 fmkorea, date unknown15.

    • A short cooldown on the gap-closer matters because staying attached to the boss keeps the 보호진 mechanic active, called "매우 좋음" (very good) inven 116, date unknown16
  5. At cap
    Rotation stays the same, only the passive and stigma spread deepens

    See Skill priority above, and the Stigma picks and Daevanion board route cards below, for the full endgame spread.

No Chanter-specific gear-while-leveling facts turned up beyond what the Gear and stat priority card below already covers, so that block is dropped here.

Healing Incantation, 16 or 20: one guide pushes it to skill Lv 20 for continuous casting, +10% max HP recovery, and a 3-second cooldown cut inven 116, date unknown17. A separate guide says stop at 16, "쾌유의 주문 20스킬 절대 찍지마라" (never spend a point past 16), matching the level-16 cap given in the Stigma picks card below from a different source, which makes 16 the better-supported number dcinside 990309, date unknown18.
Avoid: spending past skill Lv 16 on Healing Incantation on the strength of a single guide alone; the better-supported view is that the extra healing does not justify the cost past 16 dcinside 990309, date unknown19.

blocks.title: Stigma picks
blocks.headExtrasHtml: confirmed top picks kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Level Source of Invincibility to 20 first, no argument; Authority of Swiftness is next, the rest is situational.

Both Vortex Gaming guides agree strongly: Source of Invincibility is the single highest-priority stigma, called "a 1-tier stigma, no argument" and offering "substantial party and self-stat improvements," recommended to level 20 confirmed, 2 sources vortexgaming, date unknown1 vortexgaming, date unknown2.

Authority of Swiftness follows as essential, "Top Priority."

Optional and situational

  • Hand of Recovery: "very important in Transcendence," the Arcana-farming dungeon content vortexgaming, date unknown3
  • Crush, Authority of Interception, and Block: chosen by playstyle
  • Crush (reach level 5): reduces recast time and increases "Groggy Gauge" damage, per a separate guide vortexgaming, date unknown4
  • Origin of Dash (reach level 10): boosts movement speed, healing received by 5%, and stamina recovery

Korean community translation

A Korean community summary (titles and AI-summarized snippets only, not directly fetched, single source) corroborates and translates contested, single source:

  • 불패 (Invincibility/Undefeated, matches Source of Invincibility): unambiguous tier-1 stigma
  • 질주 (Dash/Sprint, likely Origin of Dash): move speed, stamina recovery, and minor HP recovery
  • 질풍 (Gale/Gust): attack speed, accuracy, crit, and cooldown reduction

The same source notes a level-5 spec on "질풍의 권능" (Power of Gale) that reduces cooldown by 20% for the whole party's skill cooldowns during the buff, not just the caster's.

A rough combat-power gate for main-healer viability, same Korean summary: "up to about 2200 combat power, having Hand of Recovery (쾌유의 주문) at level 16 is enough to work as a main healer."

This implies Chanter can substitute for Cleric below that CP threshold in undemanding content, but likely needs more investment beyond it.

Possibly Aion 1, not confirmed for AION 2: search results on stigma unlock level and Greater Stigma tiers returned original-AION sources (aion.fandom.com's Stigma Stone page, an aspirine.su stigma calculator, differ.blog) stating stigmas unlock around level 23 with up to four equipped, and that a level-45 quest unlocks two Greater Stigma slots across three grades: Normal (green), Greater (blue), Major (gold). This could not be confirmed as applying to AION 2 rather than the original AION aion fandom, date unknown5 differ.blog, date unknown6.
Gap: no Chanter-specific rule found for what to spend Stigma Shards on first, beyond the general system rule (funding equipped, main-rotation stigmas before alternates) carried over from Cleric research. No reliable source found distinguishing a clean PvE-healing/support vs solo-DPS vs PvP stigma set for Chanter.

blocks.title: Daevanion board route
blocks.bodyHtml:
Put early Daevanion points into Max Mana and Wave Strike nodes; the board system itself is shared across all classes.

The general Daevanion system (board names, node color/cost tiers) is shared across classes: Nezekan (lvl 12), Zikel (lvl 20), Vaizel (lvl 30), Triniel (lvl 40) boards, plus four level-45 advanced boards.

Grey/Green/Blue/Orange nodes cost 1/2/3/4 points respectively. No reliable source found suggesting this system differs for Chanter; see the Cleric write-up for the general mechanics.

  1. Lv 12
    Nezekan board unlocks
  2. Lv 20
    Zikel board unlocks
  3. Lv 30
    Vaizel board unlocks
  4. Lv 40
    Triniel board unlocks
  5. Lv 45
    Four advanced boards unlock

    Ariel, Azphel, Marchutan, Yustiel.

Chanter-specific guidance from one source: "Concentrate investments primarily in Max Mana and Wave Strike nodes. Select damage resistance nodes (Ariel, Aspel) if avoiding PvP content" single source vortexgaming, date unknown1.

This implies a stat-node (Max Mana) plus active-skill-node (Wave Strike, likely tied to the Dark Wave/Crushing Wave chain) route early, with Ariel and Azphel recommended for PvE-focused players seeking damage resistance over PvP-oriented boards.

Gap: no reliable source found for a full node-by-node early route, when to reset, or which of the four level-45 advanced boards is best for a PvP-leaning Chanter specifically.

blocks.title: Arcana
blocks.bodyHtml:
Two guides disagree on Chanter's Arcana card-type names and slot assignment; Vigor 4/Purity 4 is the most-recommended endgame combo.

The Arcana system overall (shared across classes): cards come from the "Transcendence" dungeon and are equipped for Combat Power, passive/active skill bonuses, skill-level transcendence, set effects, and PvE/PvP specialization bonuses expcarry, date unknown1.

Card type names

Card types named for Chanter

  • Chalice, Parchment, Compass, Bell, Mirror expcarry, date unknown2

Card types named for Cleric (for comparison)

  • Chalice, Bell, Mirror, Scales

These two lists differ. Card-type naming may be inconsistent across guide sources, or may have changed between patches. Treat as contested.

Meta-set combinations

General meta-set combinations mentioned, not confirmed Chanter-specific single source, KR-era vortexgaming, date unknown3:

  • "Frenzy 4/Purity 2" as a newbie-friendly set
  • "Vigor/Magic/Purity" for established players
  • "Vigor 4/Purity 4" as the most recommended combination
  • The broader meta reportedly shifted from "4 Vitality 1 Magic" to "3 Vitality 2 Magic" or "2 Vitality 3 Magic"

A dedicated English-language Chanter Arcana guide lays out three progressive setups single source vortexgaming, date unknown4:

  1. Beginner: Frenzy 4 / Purity 2, Grail/Parchment/Compass/Scales as Frenzy, Bell/Mirror as Purity.
  2. Intermediate: Vigor/Magic/Purity mix, Grail/Parchment as Vigor, Bell/Mirror as Magic, Compass/Scales as Purity.
  3. Most recommended, endgame: Vigor 4 / Purity 4, Grail/Parchment as Vigor, Compass/Bell/Mirror/Scales as Purity.

Two endgame combos compared

English guide (endgame combo)

  • Vigor 4 / Purity 4: Grail/Parchment as Vigor, Compass/Bell/Mirror/Scales as Purity vortexgaming, date unknown5

Korean thread (PvE combo)

  • 4 Purity (순수) + 2 Frenzy (광분): Frenzy(Time) Parchment, Frenzy(Life) Compass, Purity(Death) Bell, Purity(Destruction) Mirror, Purity(Wisdom) Scales, Purity(Destruction+Fate) fmkorea, date unknown6 kr-era

Both threads agree on the Frenzy/Purity naming (광분 = Frenzy, 순수 = Purity) but differ in exact slot assignment, suggesting the "best" combo may be patch- or preference-dependent contested.

Gap: neither source names which specific active skills Chanter should target on Chalice-equivalent cards, unlike Cleric's Chalice skill list (Forge, Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, and so on). Both sources address which stat-category (Frenzy/Purity/Vigor/Magic) goes on which slot, not which active skills to slot.
Avoid: the general system-level guidance from the Cleric-side Arcana research (presumably applicable but not independently confirmed for Chanter) is don't over-invest in expensive Vitality-type cards from scratch, and lock rather than delete old cards since metas shift with patches.

blocks.title: Gear and stat priority
blocks.bodyHtml:
Battle Chanter goes Critical Hit and Physical Attack; support Chanter goes for buff uptime and survivability over raw damage.

Weapon: Staff, used for both offense and, per one source, an in-class block mechanic, removing the need for a shield swap.

  1. Do first (offensive / "Battle Chanter"): Critical Hit and Physical Attack for damage per hit and faster mob clearing, plus Critical Hit and Accuracy so crowd-control effects land reliably single source aggregation.
  2. Then (support Chanter): gear that "enhances your support toolkit" over top-tier DPS stats, since "your value comes from survivability and consistent buff uptime."
  3. Later / optional: a note of uncertain provenance for AION 2 suggests Magic Boost is only a secondary stat for Chanter, since the class is fundamentally physical low confidence, possible AION 1 conflation
    • Possibly carried over from original-AION guidance.
    • Physical Attack, Critical Hit, and Attack Speed are the suggested primary stats.

aion2boost.com's build philosophy: "Uptime matters most, a weaker buff maintained consistently outperforms a stronger one that lapses," implying Cooldown Reduction and buff-duration stats should be weighed alongside raw damage stats for a support-oriented Chanter aion2boost, date unknown1.

Gap: no reliable source found for which specific gear piece to enhance first for Chanter, nor for named set-effect gear pieces (unlike Cleric, no player-submitted example build page was found). No reliable source found for a manastone/godstone-equivalent socketing system specific to Chanter.

blocks.title: Rotation and combos
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested naming single source
blocks.bodyHtml:
Rotation names are contested across guides; the constant is mantra upkeep, recast them immediately after every death.

Solo PvE rotation (aggregated guide, lower trust)

  1. Engage with CC.
  2. Apply Strike Chain for guaranteed stun and damage over time.
  3. Cleave with Ascendant Strike.
  4. Drop a regen zone for sustain.
  5. Repeat the rotation.
Naming conflict: these skill names (Strike Chain, Ascendant Strike) do not match the Dark Wave/Crushing Wave/Back Breaker names from the Vortex skill-tree guides, likely reflecting different translation passes or patch versions rather than confirmed distinct skill lists. Treat exact skill names as provisional.

A second phrasing closer to AION2 Hub's own description: open with staff combos including Onslaught, Resonance Crush, Impactful Crush, and Crushing Blow to apply physical damage and debuffs, while "life-leech and stat-boosting mantras" maintain party viability aion2hub, date unknown1.

Again this skill-name set does not overlap cleanly with the Vortex guide's names.

Animation canceling combo single source: "Crushing Wave and then use a skill based on left-click or Source of Recovery" is cited as a rapid-execution animation-cancel sequence; the guide itself stresses this reflects "personal opinion and not the definitive answer" vortexgaming, date unknown2.

Mantra and party rhythm

Mantra/aura upkeep moderate confidence, single source: Chanter's signature mechanic is the mantra system, buffs that are instantly cast, persist until manually cancelled or replaced (not on a timer, and "cannot be dispelled by any means"), and act as an aura benefiting the whole nearby group by proximity.

  • Up to three mantras can be active solo, or four if grouped with a second Chanter.
  • This may partly describe original-AION mantra mechanics carried into AION 2.
  • Party composition should steer mantra choice: a caster-heavy party benefits from magic-boosting mantras, a melee-heavy party benefits from physical attack power/critical rate mantras.
Beginner tip: always recast mantras immediately after death/respawn, since they drop and are not automatically restored.
Gap: no reliable source found with a named Chanter defensive cooldown analogous to Cleric's Immortal Curtain, or a confirmed auto-hunt skill setup for Chanter.

blocks.title: Leveling notes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Chanter levels solo just fine numerically, but its buffing identity only shows up in a group.

Solo leveling comfort is generally rated positively for raw survival and clear speed, "fast mob clearing and excellent sustainability" thanks to built-in sustain and crowd control marketing, lower trust.

But aion2boost.com's more skeptical framing should be weighed against this: Chanter's identity is built around buffing others, so solo leveling, while numerically fine, does not showcase the class's actual strength and may feel comparatively flat next to classes fully usable alone aion2boost, date unknown1.

Sustain: regen zones plus life-leech mantras give consistent self-sustain without heavy potion use, similar in spirit to Cleric's self-healing but delivered as an AoE zone rather than an instant heal.

This means Chanter benefits from standing in its own zone rather than kiting constantly (inferred from Fextralife's "lacks instant single-target heals but excels with AoE regeneration zones" note, moderate confidence).

"Turns on" point: aion2boost.com's grading suggests Chanter turns on specifically when joining an organized/premade group rather than at any particular character level or gear milestone; its value is structurally tied to having allies present to buff.

Gap: no reliable source found for a specific level or CP number where Chanter's personal (non-buff) power spikes, beyond the single Korean-community note that roughly 2200 combat power is enough to function as a main-healer substitute in easier content. No reliable source found for specific mob-density or pulling-size comfort numbers.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Fight in melee range with your group, keep mantras up, and never play Chanter like a ranged Cleric.

Do

  • Stay in melee range, fight with your group, and amplify everyone around you pvpbank, date unknown1
  • Pre-place AoE healing/regeneration zones where the team is stacked
  • Recast Mantras every time after respawning
  • Play close to the tank, you are strongest in the center of the fight
  • Prioritize survivability first, damage second, a dead Chanter provides no buffs to anyone
  • Keep a weaker buff up consistently rather than chase a marginally stronger one that lapses (aion2boost.com's build philosophy)
  • Recognize the class's grade is roster-dependent, lean into premade/organized groups

Do not

  • Play Chanter like a Cleric, standing at range and healing pvpbank, date unknown2
  • Spam direct heals instead of placing healing zones
  • Forget to recast mantras after dying
  • Stay too far from the tank/fight
  • Prioritize personal damage over survivability and buff uptime
  • Chase mantra swaps so aggressively that uptime drops
  • Neglect the Hand of Recovery / Huyu's Spell recovery line while over-investing in the damage chain, undermining the "never the main healer, yet able to keep a group standing" identity
